To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) deep residual networks are sufficient to solve a variety of time series forecasting problems; (ii) deep residual networks can be augmented with a small number of interpretable components that can provide a meaningful explanation of the forecast; and (iii) a deep neural architecture that is both interpretable and accurate can be trained very efficiently, which is important for practical applications.

1) deep learning models based on residual connections and a very deep fully-connected stack of layers, without any time-series specific components, can solve a wide range and variety of forecasting problems; 2) the model can be augmented to be interpretable without a significant loss in performance.

(1) deep learning primitives such neural residual blocks and deep fully connected layers, without any time-series-specific modifications, can be successfully used to forecast time series; (2) the resulting architecture, called N-BEATS, is fast to train, easy to interpret, and achieves state-of-the-art results on a wide range of datasets.
